summary:
Evaluate expression `expr`. Return 0 if it completes without an error. A driver runtime error is returned as a string beginning with `*` and containing the error message.

   throw(value) stops the current execution and transfers value to the nearest enclosing catch(). throw() itself never returns; that catch() returns the thrown value unchanged. The value can have any type and is not converted to text. A thrown string does not receive the leading asterisk used for driver errors. Throwing 0 is indistinguishable from normal completion.

   catch is a compiler directive (or a language construct, as it is called in PHP), rather than an efun. Other examples include sscanf, time_expression, and parse_command.
